simple.meaning: דָּפַק (dâphaq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to knock ; by analogy, to press severely.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Genesis, Judges, Song of Solomon, beginning at Genesis 33:13. Its contexts include flock, kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דָּפַק (H1849).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: דָּפַק (dâphaq) / H1849 is traced through Genesis 33:13, Judges 19:22, Song of Songs 5:2 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to knock ; by analogy, to press severely
definitions.full: H1849. daphaq [ דָּפַק ] verb beat, knock (Arabic pour out , also drive (beasts)) — Qal Perf. 3masculine plural suffix וּדְפָקוּם consecutive Gen 33:13 , but read 1singular suffix ᵑ6 ᵐ5 וּדְפַקְתִּים Sam Di beat (in driving, drive severely or cruelly); Participle דּוֺפֵק Song 5:2 absolute knocking (at door). Hithpa`el Participle עַלהַֿדָּ֑לֶת מִתְדַּמְּקִים Judg 19:22 beat violently (beat themselves tired) against the door.
